text: hey everybody every last word of the Bible is historically and socially and rhetorically contingent what that means is that every last word of the Bible was
written by a person or a group of people in a specific time and place because of a specific set of circumstances and in
order to achieve a specific set of rhetorical goals and those goals were always aimed at those specific sets of
circumstances in other words no word of the Bible actually trans sends the
circumstances of its composition and when we try to compel the words of the Bible to transcend the circumstances of
their composition that is something that we are imposing upon the Bible from the outside and there are some interesting
implications of this because many texts from the Bible disagree with each other and are aimed at different rhetorical
goals when we impose the assumption that they transcend their settings we must must erase the intentions of the authors
frequently in order to harmonize the text to make them agree and have the appearance of univocality but the Bible
is not univocal additionally because we can only achieve that univocality and modern application of a lot of these
things by imposing these assumptions upon the text and by altering what the text was intended to convey and
accomplish there is no such thing as the Bible says so there is only what we have negotiated with the Bible and that
negotiation is driven by whatever will make the Bible more meaningful or more useful to the individuals and the groups
reading it today there's no such thing as the Bible says so there is only we say so and we want the Bible to be our
